articleTitle: Application of Power Routers in Standalone Power Systems
abstract: The contemporary power generation is characterized by changing the technological platform while performing a transition to smart grids technologies whose key elements are distributed generation (DG) plants and electrical energy storage units. Pilot projects of such grids can be implemented in standalone power systems while using DG plants operating on renewable energy sources. The prospective lines, ensuring efficient use of the DG plants in standalone energy systems, is formation of energy microgrids that allow combining the DG and energy storage units based on special interfaces. Power routers can be used as such interfaces which are built based on high-frequency solid state transformers with two active semiconductor bridges.The article presents power router models, DG plants based on renewable energy sources and electrical energy storage units, based on which the standalone power system microgrid is formed. The research was carried out with application of simulation modeling packages Simulink and SimPowerSystems of MATLAB system. The modeling results allow to formulate conclusions that the power router designed based on a solid state transformer with active double bridge can be used to generate standalone power system energy microgrid. When main power is interrupted and is transferred to a standby power supply due to the use of power router, DC and AC consumers operate steadily due to the absence of significant voltage dips.

articleTitle: Cuckoo search algorithm for optimal siting and sizing of multiple distributed generators in distribution grids
abstract: Distribution networks (DNs) are facing numerous challenges such as variability of demands, environmental issues, high power losses, and fluctuating voltage profiles. Distributed energy resources (DERs) are becoming more important due to their economic and environmental impacts. This paper presents optimal siting and sizing of the Photovoltaics (PVs) and Wind Turbines (WTs) to improve the voltage magnitude profiles. This planning problem is formulated using DER generation and load profiles of the three representative days, one for each season. The resulting constrained optimization problem is solved using Cuckoo Search Algorithm (CSA). The proposed solution approach is applied to the 33 bus and 69 bus radial distribution networks. Several simulations are performed for the performance analysis of the methods and the results are compared to several available ones.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of challenges for power system protection – selected aspects of transformation of power systems
abstract: The European electrical power system is facing a number of challenges. These challenges are determined by the currently observed and expected future directions of the development of European power systems. Identification of these challenges was performed. In the analysis, different perspectives of perception of power system as a reference point were assumed. The analysis included not only technical aspects, but also formal and legal factors, social expectations, economic challenges, security requirements, energy independence, etc. This allowed identifying the most important factors. They may change the model of operation of power systems. The publication focuses on the characterization of the most important factors identified as these which may cause the necessity to change the current approach to power system protection.

articleTitle: Reliability Enhancement of High Voltage Power Transformer Using Online Oil Dehydration
abstract: Electrical system reliability is highly dependent on power transformers performance. Yet the transformer reliability is highly impacted by its cooling medium and the contaminants within the cooling medium. These contaminants account for roughly 15% of transformer failures. Contaminants such as water can be harmful to the transformer, will reduce its reliability, and, consequently, the electrical system reliability. Therefore, moisture must be eliminated from the cooling medium as well as the insulation paper of the transformer. In this paper, an online oil drying system technology is implemented on a 69/13.8 kV transformer with more than 35 years in service. The technology removes moistures from transformer’s oil and the winding insulation paper. This paper also illustrate the working principle of this technology. The importance of this technology comes from the fact that the drying process is conducted while the power transformer is in service. Hence, no outage is required. The ultimate purpose of transformer dehydration is to increase the transformer reliability and extend its service life. This paper analyzes the performance of the online dehydration technology and compares it to offline methods. Actual oil analysis results show that this dehydration system reduced the water content in the insulation medium by 29%.

articleTitle: Data Processing in IoT Systems based on Fuzzy Logics
abstract: Analysis of the parameters that influence to the quality and efficiency of data transferring in complex decision making systems was performed. Increasing of exactness and adequacy of data processing in IoT system could be achieved by use of fuzzy logic approach with modified method of fuzzy rules and base of knowledge forming. Repeats and conflict management for logical rules is described. Realization of proposed approach on the base of cloud service provide efficient work and possibility to modify initial knowledge base.

articleTitle: A Simulation Model for Evaluation of Intersystem Fault in a Hybrid AC/DC Power System and its impact on the Protection System
abstract: Due to increasing environmental burden and other cost related reasons, the transmission network is undergoing major change globally. One way to utilize transmission corridors more efficiently is to have several three-phase systems in the same tower. This can be multiple AC and DC circuits or AC circuits with different system voltages. The transmission of DC and AC on one tower is a challenging technical territory, particularly in case of intersystem faults. In order to cope with this, new technical solutions are required as well as practical testing of the present protection ideas are needed. This paper presents a PSCAD simulation model in order to investigate the intersystem faults in a hybrid AC/DC line, by utilizing four different cases. These cases have been tested to validate the simulation model and the results are presented. The arising phenomena especially the consequences with respect to the protection systems are discussed.

articleTitle: Short Term Load Forecasting for Individual Consumers based on Markov Chains
abstract: Emerging smart-grid applications in low-voltage systems generate a need to forecast not only aggregated load profiles, b ut i ndividual, c onsumer s pecific pr ofiles in a high temporal resolution. These load profiles a re n oisy a nd volatile, which makes forecasting them challenging. A short term load forecasting (STLF) model, based on Markov chains, is presented in this paper. It is designed for continuous training during operation and can be pre-trained, making it universally applicable. Its performance is evaluated at a synthetic dataset of individual households. The predictive accuracy of the model is investigated for different forecasting resolutions and levels of load aggregation. The results show that the general characteristics of individual, high resolution load profiles i s m odelled reasonably well, outperforming a naive prediction, utilizing a scaled standard load profile.

articleTitle: Short-term Load Forecasting System for Smartgrids based on Personal Power Units
abstract: Popularization of personal low-power renewable energy sources and storages application led to the appearance of flexible energy markets. When implementing a high-efficiency model of electric power trading the demand for proper assessment of the balance between consumed and produced energy becomes the biggest and the most important challenge for research. The proposed structure of microgrid system is based essentially on the combined use of personal power units and hardware-software complex built on Internet of Things (IoT), MultiAgent (MAS) and Machine Learning (ML) technologies. The main objective of that complex is an adjustment of each consumer's expected daily load curve in accordance with a number of external factors. The data obtained are used for the further formation of the agent's logic, which are carrying out the buy & sell process of electric energy for the benefit of every consumer. The transaction control role falls on each participant in the market. This solution makes it possible to organize the distributed self-regulated market of electric energy and computing resources to ensure the high-effective and reliable power supplying of microgrid participants with minimal involvement from both outer power grid, and the consumers.

articleTitle: Power System Event Detection using Auto-encoders and the Fourier Transform
abstract: Access to raw substation data in a digital form allows atypical events, which could potentially be indicative of future performance degradation or fault occurrence, to be identified. Methods where the storage of relevant data is triggered after an event has been detected can significantly reduce the amount of data to be stored. In order to propose such a system it is necessary to automatically detect power system events. In this paper, several algorithms for event or anomaly detection in electrical power systems are investigated and compared. The proposed algorithms utilize unsupervised training of auto-encoders and Fourier transform-based signal reconstruction. The algorithms are tested on a hand crafted benchmark signal, simulation-generated transients during typical faults and on available recorded events. The performance of the algorithms is compared with respect to event detection sensitivity and computational power required to run each algorithm in real time.

articleTitle: CGMES as an interface for multilateral grid modelling data exchange
abstract: Common Information Model (CIM) is an important framework used to describe electrical power systems at different voltage levels, widely applied both in the area of event message exchange and in network topology and parameter exchange. Common Grid Model Exchange Specification (CGMES) is a superset of CIM, developed specifically to meet needs of ENTSO-E, related to coordination of different actions performed by Transmission System Operators (TSO) working in the reality of interconnected and interdependent pan-European power grid. It works as vendor-independent interface between European Network of Transmission System Operators for Electricity (ENTSO-E) members, allowing them to exchange modelling information and perform common studies, despite their reliance on different analytical applications.This article is meant to work as an introduction to CGMES, its history, current place in ENTSO-E business processes, results of interoperability test and paths for further development. Key concepts in power system modelling for interconnected transmission systems are presented, including centrally maintained Boundary profiles, model authority sets (MAS), usage of globally unique master resource identifiers (mRID), profile-based model exchange and processing.

articleTitle: Computational Features of Numerical Simulation of Some Transitions in Electric Power Systems
abstract: Study of transitional processes in electric power systems being one of the main factors determining their reliability, is one of the most important problems for researchers working in area of power electrical engineering. Rapid developing of software of engineering problems and hardware, taken place for the last few decades significantly widens numerical research capabilities. Presently numerical modeling and computer simulation are widely used as primary research tool for the most of engineering problems. Therefore, ensuring the adequacy of mathematical models requires a comprehensive study of the features of simulation tools in relation to the problems to be solved. The switching transitional processes in high-voltage systems are formalized in mathematical models as the system of first order “stiff” differential and algebraic-differential equations with nonlinearity and some logical conditions for setting current interruptions (current chopping) and arc's repeated restrikes and re-ignitions, that determines complexity of the problem. Some computational features in MATLAB set of the problem under consideration conditioned by the methods (ode solvers) and algorithms (fast and robust ones) used, impact of some physical phenomena and parameters and also influence of type of circuit-breaker (vacuum and SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>) on transitional voltages' behavior and stability of solutions are generalizes and presented in this paper. The classical and modern concepts of differential equations' stiffness being a priori criterion of stability are also briefly characterized in the paper. All the researches' results and conclusions were obtained by the working up of numerous acts of computer simulation carried out in wide ranges of initial step size and relative tolerance.

articleTitle: Operational degradation of HTS tape parameters used in SFCL and its impact on the coordination of power system protection
abstract: The article presents the results of experimental investigations on HTS tapes intended for the construction of superconducting fault current limiter (SFCL). The influence of repeated exiting of HTS tape from the superconducting state by the surge current to the stability of the critical current value for HTS 2G superconducting tape type CF has been checked. The influence of the amount of energy released during the tape shock with insulation and without electrical insulation on the stability of the tape parameters was investigated. The obtained results indicate that as a result of thermal and dynamic processes occurring during the operation of the limiter, the tape parameters may be degraded and the value of the critical current may decrease. Degradation of the tape and reduction of the critical current value may result in disturbed coordination of the power system protection (PSP) settings with the SFCL parameters. The influence of degradation of HTS tapes on the coordination of PSP settings was analyzed.

articleTitle: Experiences with Double- and Single-Ended Fault Location in Compensated Network Applaying Travelling Wave Technology
abstract: This paper presents the experiences with travelling wave technology for fault location in compensated and isolated power grids [1]. Moreover, the installed pilot monitoring system as well as the background of the fault location with travelling waves is presented in detail. Some typical cases of successful fault locating and the potential of collecting additional information from the captured records is discussed. This is the first time the travelling wave technology is applied successfully for the localization of short-term single phase-to-earth faults in a compensated network.

articleTitle: Transmission Line Modelling and Simulating for Transient Analysis
abstract: In modern power systems, more and more, protection and control applications use travelling wave theory as the main criterion of operation. Therefore, more detailed and advanced models of power system components, taking into account transient states, are needed to design, develop and test these applications properly. The paper concerns the problem of transmission line modelling for transient simulations and analysis. In the introduction, a short literature review about travelling wave theory applications is presented. Theory of the method of calculating electrical parameters using physical parameters of transmission lines is described at the beginning of the paper. Next, models of transmission lines, prepared using calculated electrical parameters and tested using ATP-EMTP software, for various parameters, are presented. Conclusions from performed studies are in the last paragraph.

articleTitle: Metaidentification of the Modern Polish Power Exchange Control System
abstract: The paper contains selected results of metaidentification of the control system of the Polish Power Exchange using numerical data quoted on the Day-Ahead Market obtained in the form of a MISO metamodel. Identification methods, including methods leading to parametric models, have been used for many years, especially in technical sciences, including management and control of the power system and its subsystems. Various methods of obtaining metamodels depending on the test object are used. There are no available methods of metaidentification of technical and technical-economic systems leading directly to the metamodel of systems such as the system of the Polish Power Exchange, and the models obtained so far have been prognostic, planning or programming models.

articleTitle: Energy management in a real microgrid with hydroelectric power plant and battery storage unit
abstract: The paper presents a simulation of the energy storage power control following predefined charge characteristics. The demand of local power consumers exceeding the given margin should be covered by the local generation (hydroelectric power plant) and from an energy storage system. The energy storage unit can be charged by the energy generated by the power plant and the energy from the power system. A storage control scenario was developed, where the main goal is to limit to the set level of power exchanged with the power system. Simulation calculations were carried out using data recorded in a real power system. The paper shows the influence of selection of energy storage unit characteristics and different generation cases on the operation of the whole system.

articleTitle: Elimination of Aperiodic Components of Measuring Elements of Relay Protection
abstract: In this paper, we propose algorithms to calculate the actual values of currents and their derivatives. The algorithms allow a sharp reduction in the aperiodic components of currents in the calculated actual values and their derivatives. Algorithms are developed to calculate the instantaneous values of positive- and negative-sequence currents when the information obtained during a time interval equal to two sinusoidal components of the currents in the presence of aperiodic components in the samples. To eliminate the disoperation of digital relay protection and improve the accuracy of fault location, it is necessary to eliminate the influence of aperiodic components in the currents drawn to the measuring devices of relay protection. The algorithm completely eliminates the aperiodic component at any time constants and is implemented by four samples of currents. The four samples of currents separated by three sampling intervals are sufficient for calculating all the parameters of currents, including the positive and negative-sequence currents, in particular in the case when the magnetic cores of current transformers reach saturation. The proposed methods for setting the industrial frequency parameters to avoid the aperiodic components in short-circuit currents are based on the algorithms that process the data from three and four samples of currents.

articleTitle: Consumers IED - Power Management by Smart Meter
abstract: Smart metering technologies are evolving at a pace with modern trends in the power industry. Additional useful properties of electric energy accounting systems are the ability to manage the load and build relationships between consumers with their own generation and passive consumers in microgrids.

articleTitle: An Evaluation of Remanent Flux of Autotransformer on Resonant Overvoltage
abstract: Abnormal resonant overvoltages occur due to the emergence of non-sinusoidal modes of bulk electrical networks. The considered type of overvoltage refers to durable internal overvoltages, which have characteristics that can exceed the maximum permissible magnitude with a certain correlation of the values of the parameters of the extra high voltage power transmission line 750 kV. A typical example of a non-sinusoidal mode of operation of an extra high voltage line is the mode of switching on the line to an unloaded autotransformer. It should be noted that this mode is accompanied not only by resonant overvoltages, but also by inrush currents of magnetization. As a result, modern developers of controlled switching devices should choose switch-on settings for successful solution of two tasks: suppression of inrush current and resonant overvoltage. The paper analyzes the effect of remanent magnetization of an unloaded autotransformer on resonant overvoltages. To remove the remanent magnetization of the autotransformer, a set of effective measures for suppressing resonant overvoltages has been proposed.

articleTitle: Method and algorithm of control of shunt reactors of high-voltage power network in maintenance modes based on fuzzy logic theory
abstract: Stable connections of power grid with other power systems, their parallel operation or the creation of nonsynchronous communication by means of a DC device are important conditions for a highly perspective stable power supply. The analysis and study of the problems arising during the application of modern technologies to ensure the power grid reliability are topical in adjustment of frequency, voltage and capacity to ensure the regime reliability on such power route. From this point of view, in high-voltage system-forming and inter-system electrical networks, it is of particular importance to conduct research on the forming of a control system based on modern technologies, the placement of FACTS devices in the part of control shunt reactors (CSR) to compensate the charging capability. Thus, in high-voltage system-forming and inter-system electric networks, the use of charging capability compensation means for power transmission lines (PTL) creates an opportunity to ensure a sufficiently high reliability and efficiency of the power system mode. On both sides of 500 kV PTL of the power grid, relevant research work was carried out in connection with the placement and control of the FACTS devices of CSR. These works represent the research related to the development and implementation of the methods and algorithms of CSR control mainly on the basis of traditional and non-traditional mathematical technologies. However, in the works under consideration the questions of adequacy of planned and unplanned switch-ons of system elements (power lines, generators, transformers) of the given methods and algorithms were considered insufficiently. This work represents the results of the development and computer implementation of the methods and algorithms for controlling the CSR device in the state of shift switch-ons (N-1 criterion) of the power grid elements using the mathematical fuzzy logic apparatus. The obtained results confirm the reactive power compensation and bus voltage stabilization during its controlling high-voltage networks during the short-term plannings of maintenance modes and, therefore, the possibility of provision for the power grid voltage stability.

articleTitle: Hybrid Approach for Short-term Wind Power Prediction to Increase Flexibility of Renewable Integration in Power System
abstract: Renewable energy (RE) is rapidly increasing as an alternative to conventional power systems. One of the examples is the power system of Krabi province in the south of Thailand, whose 2026 projected energy consumption, is expected to be met almost entirely by RE sources. Generation from these volatile renewable sources largely depends on the weather, which causes problems on the transmission, e.g., the excess power flow reversing or backfeeding, and the 1ack of production or shortage. These problems cause particular difficulty in the wind power prediction of the power operation system in planning the future schedule. Consequently, inaccuracy of generating future scheduling diminishes the flexibility of the power system. In this paper, we describe a system to mitigate the problems by proposing a hybrid model of wind power prediction combining long short-term memory (LSTM) and Markov chain (MC) with quantization (QTZ) and denoising (DN) techniques. The experimental results show that the hybrid model increases the accuracy of the wind power prediction.

articleTitle: Assessment of Available Measurement Data, Data Breaks and Estimation of Missing Data from AMI Meters
abstract: Paper presents problems connected with collection, initial processing and validation of data from smart electric meters AMI installed in energy consumption points. Collected data should be then identified and classified. If the lack of data was detected they should be adequately estimated. Extreme disturbances in data sequences should be reduced too. The around-the-clock loads profiles are modelled on base of recorded and processed measurements. Verified profiles are used in estimation of missing data. The methods of modelling the around-the-clock loads profiles as well as the possibilities and methods of using the obtained models in estimation of missing data presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Analysis of Voltage Dip Source Location Methods
abstract: The voltage dip is one of the prominent disturbances in power systems related to power quality. Therefore it is very important to investigate the methods which allow to determine voltage dip direction finder. In this work selected voltage dip source location methods are discussed and investigated. The analysis are performed in Matlab Simulink environment. The methods are tested using different kind of fault and different fault location. The dip direction is indicated using two selected methods based on analysis of energy and impedance variation during the disturbance. The methods are applied for the measurements aggregated in different nodes of power systems, representing supply and customer side respectively. Based on the results of the dip direction achieved by investigated methods a general conclusions are formulated about the correctness, advantages and disadvantages of the discussed methods.

articleTitle: Development and validation of a neural network for state estimation in the distribution grid based on μPMU data
abstract: The increased expansion of decentralised renewable energy resources (DER), such as photovoltaic (PV) systems, and private charging points for electric vehicles (EV) with high charging capacities of up to 22 kW pose new challenges for distribution grid operators in Germany. In Germany, both DER and EVs are installed in the electrical grid primarily at the low-voltage level. In order to ensure grid stability in the future, energy generation by DER and charging of EVs must be coordinated locally. At the low-voltage level, however, there is mainly no measurement technology installed which is required for the implementation of a grid-compatible control of the charge EVs and feed-in of DER. It is not economical to equip every grid node with measurement technology. The paper presents an artificial neural network (ANN) which is trained by means of the voltage data of a software image of a real low-voltage grid and which subsequently estimates the voltage of all nodes of the grid section on the basis of a few measuring points in the real low-voltage grid. The ANN has been developed and validated in software. An average accuracy of the actual node voltage to the estimated node voltage of the ANN of 4.29 V mean absolute error, 1.23 % mean absolute percentage error and 4.49 V root mean square error has been achieved.

articleTitle: Grid Steady State Evaluation for Stochastic Nature of Renewables and Loads
abstract: The development of the electric power industry for the next 20-30 years provides a significant growth of generation from renewable sources, as well as improvement of the efficiency of distribution and consumer electric networks. In the structure of renewable generation, the output from wind and solar power plants generally exceeds the output from other renewable sources. The probabilistic-fuzzy nature of wind power and solar plants, as well as the stochasticity of the load power leads to random variability of voltage and power flows in the electrical networks of the system. The effect of random-indefinite variability of mode in the network may increase with the growth of power from wind and solar plants integrated into the system. In this paper we propose probabilistic fuzzy models that describe the power system state variability caused by the load and generation stochasticity. The proposed models are presented in the form of the Gauss fuzzy description with varying center and width for the membership functions of the mode parameters that determine the system state. It is shown that the proposed models allow for approximating the current and forecasting values of its parameters with a higher accuracy on the basis of simultaneous consideration of stochasticity and uncertainty in the variability of the power system state. The paper consists of introduction, which formulates the problem of modeling of the power system state, taking into account the stochasticity and uncertainty of its variability, in the form of a probabilistic fuzzy set; in the second section the procedure for the identifying the model structure of the probabilistic fuzzy set in relation to the description of the random variability of the system state caused by the load power stochasticity is proposed; in the third section an analysis of the simulation results of the power system state represented by the fuzzy description for the voltage vector and power flows in the network is provided.

articleTitle: A reliability-transient stability analysis of power systems for protection system conditions
abstract: This study introduces a transient stability-reliability analysis considering the effects of protection system operation. The analysis considers both the deterministic and the probabilistic parameters. Once the protection system conditions and their parameters are identified, deterministic and probabilistic transition rates are used in order to calculate the transient and steady-state reliability measures using the Markov model of the process. Some transient stability parameters of a specific fault in the system, such as critical fault clearing time and oscillation finishing time are used to determine some deterministic transition rates. For reliability analysis, state probabilities, Loss of Load Expectation, Expected Energy Not Served are calculated for several contingency scenarios taking into account the power flow results obtained by Newton Raphson method. Finally, risk analysis is performed and compared for the aforementioned contingency scenarios. The proposed model is tested on WECC-9 bus system and the results are illustrated.

articleTitle: Modern single-ended fault location in HVDC systems based on fault transients
abstract: This paper presents a single-ended method for fault location in HVDC segmented transmission line consisted of two segments, overhead and cable. The challenge for fault location is to use one terminal measurement data without using communication channel and synchronization links between measurements of two terminals. The proposed method is based on extracting traveling wave impulses from measured transients and matching them with referenced time schemes obtained using Bewley's lattice diagrams crated on the basis of parameters of segmented line. Generated Bewley's diagrams are treated as data base of fault finger prints. The aim function is to achieve the best matching of finger print and extracted measured transients. Presented method is investigated using real measurements of Baltic Sweden-Germany HVDC power transmission link during staged fault tests and decaying fault. Obtained results shows that proposed method is capable for locating the faults and introduce new solution for single-ended technique in segmented HVDC transmission lines.

articleTitle: Improving Handling of Shunt-Reactor Effects during Fault with Focus on Protection Devices
abstract: In this paper, the application of the shunt-reactor on the line, its advantages and disadvantages are discussed with relevant calculations and simulations. The paper also presents modeling, dimensioning and location issues of shunt-reactors. This depth is necessary for the understanding of problems which can occur in protection devices. The paper proposes possible solutions of these issues and presents the derivation of the proposed approach. Application of the described solution guarantees more reliability of protection operation on lines with shunt reactors.

articleTitle: Integrated Simulation Environment for Investigation of Multi-Agent Systems in Smart Grids Applications
abstract: This paper presents a framework for simulation environment for modelling and testing smart grids controlled by multi agent systems. The environment is based on the co-simulation approach and consists of MATLAB/Simulink, where the power grid part is modelled, Java Agent DEvelopment framework, where the multi-agent system is programmed, and the interface between these two based on TCP/IP communication. The interface is designed to be general and it can be used also for purposes other than power systems application. Structure, integration within both ends, and functioning of the interface is the main focus of this paper.

articleTitle: The problem of selected parameters of the power quality in the perspective of tightening normative requirements
abstract: The article presents a method of evaluating the electricity quality parameter based on the applicable regulations and in accordance with the perspective of forthcoming changes that tighten normative requirements. The quality of electricity was assessed on the basis of the flicker factor. The article presents the effects of not providing adequate quality of electricity.

articleTitle: Value- Based Real Time Reactive Power Pricing Model Considering Voltage Security and Reserve Requirement
abstract: Reactive power service is considered as an important ancillary service, due to its contribution towards maintaining system wide bus voltage. In this work, a value based reactive power pricing model suitable for real time market is proposed. In the proposed reactive power market model, bids(operation cost and lost opportunity cost(LOC) of reactive power) are received from the Generating Companies (GENCOs) participating in the real time market. From the bids received, a three component reactive power value function is formulated. The components of value function being load serving component, voltage support component and reserve component of reactive power requirement in the system. The objective of the Independent System Operator (ISO) is to minimise the value function of reactive power requirement in the system subject to generator limits, bus voltage limits and transmission line limits. From the Lagrange function of the optimisation problem, the marginal value (MV) of reactive power is derived to calculate the marginal price (MP) of reactive power. The NLP formulation of the market model is solved using DICOPT solver in GAMS and anlaysed on IEEE 24-Bus system. The simulation results prove that the proposed algorithm is efficient in clearing the reactive power market in such a way that the system wide bus voltage deviation is minimal and sufficient reactive power reserve is maintained in the network.

articleTitle: Analysis of Power Transformer Magnetizing Inrush and Overexcitation Conditions in Case of Overvoltages due to Line-to-Ground Fault
abstract: In this paper, simulation of power transformer operation during external phase-to-ground faults are presented, with special attention paid to the overvoltage, magnetizing inrush and overexcitation conditions due to such faults. The motivation for conducted studies were recorded cases of maloperation of transformer differential protection during external faults. The paper starts with initial analysis of the recorded cases. Then developed model of the network with protected transformer is described and verified by simulations with MATLAB/Simulink software. Theoretical and simulation investigations lead to observations related to the level of overvoltage and harmonic content in the currents during considered faults, as well as reasons of protection wrong operation. Discussion about the possibility of harmonic blocking application concludes the paper.

articleTitle: Virtual Inertia Implementation in Variable Speed Hydropower Plant
abstract: This paper investigates how a variable speed hydropower (VSHP) plant with virtual inertia (VI) control can deliver fast power reserves to compensate for variable production of renewables and maintain grid stability after disturbances. The advantage of the VSHP is that it is able to change the electric power output significantly within a few seconds and maintaining it for a longer period. During the first seconds, the energy is taken from the rotating masses in the generator and the turbine. Thereafter, the water flow and thereby the mechanical power are adjusted by governor action to return the turbine to its optimal speed. Two VI control structures are implemented and tested on a VSHP plant simulation model. The virtual synchronous generator (VSG) and the virtual synchronous machine (VSM) are further developed to fulfil the main objective of the control; to maximize the grid support from the VSHP by utilizing the turbine and generator rotational energy. At the same time, the impact on the hydraulic system must be considered in order to fulfil the objectives for internal control of the plant; i.e. to optimize the turbine rotational speed, minimize water hammering and mass oscillations, minimize guide vane servo operation and minimize hydraulic and electric losses. Dynamic analyses are performed to compare the control structures; the power-frequency PID controller with permanent droop (VSG-PID) based on the VSG and the VSM with powerfrequency PID controller and permanent droop (VSM-PID). They are evaluated by two main criteria; their ability to deliver instantaneous power (inertia) to reduce the rate of change of frequency (ROCOF) and their contribution to frequency containment control (steady state frequency droop response).

articleTitle: Simulation of the Power Transmission Lines Electrical Field to Ensure Safe Navigation of the Unmanned Aerial Vehicles at Their Monitoring
abstract: One of the modern methods of power transmission lines (PTLs) monitoring is usage of the unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). For the UAVs operation PTLs electromagnetic field (EMF) levels can be used. For calculation of electrical field strength, PTLs wires were replaced by parallel to the earth surface infinitely long cylinders, along which axes charge is distributed with the same density. Both analytical and numerical solutions have been used. At numerical approach, influence of PTLs towers has been regarded. Such calculations were used for obtaining of the PTLs EF strengths distributions, as well as their gradients in the area lateral and upward to the PTLs wires and towers. Such distributions permit appreciation of the safe and unsafe zones of UAVs operation from the point of view of electromagnetic compatibility of the UAVs' electronic equipment with the PTLs EF.

articleTitle: Design of an inverter model according to the network code requirements for low-voltage grids
abstract: One of the most challenging aspects of controlling microgrids is islanding and resynchronization with the grid. During this process, unwanted disconnection of inverters due to voltage fluctuations or frequency deviations may occur. In order to investigate these phenomena in more detail, inverter models are required, which support the corresponding protective functions. This work describes a concept for modelling an inverter in accordance with the minimum technical requirements for connection and parallel operation of generating plants on the low-voltage grid in Germany for future investigation of the islanding and resynchronization process of microgrids.

articleTitle: Intelligent Aggregated Load Management System
abstract: Development of the industry is increasingly transforming the topology of power systems. The more acutely issues of uninterrupted operation are raised. An intelligent control method using trend technologies that supports power supply without complicating the network configuration is proposed in the article.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Results and Potential Cost of the Polish Capacity Market Auctions in 2018
abstract: The article presents results of first auctions of the Polish capacity market. Those results were analysed in terms of the number of individual types of Capacity Market Units (CMU), and then the percentage share of individual capital groups in the amount of contracted capacity was indicated. In addition, the potential cost of introducing the capacity market was calculated and compared with the potential cost originally assumed by the Ministry of Energy. The results of the auctions confirmed that the targets set in the Capacity Market Act will be achieved. Thanks to the capacity market financing, energy groups will want to build almost 5 GW of new generation capacity and almost 7.5 GW of existing generation capacity to be refurbished.

articleTitle: Hybrid predictive models dedicated to wind farms
abstract: The article describes, on the example of an inland wind farm, the possibility of forecasting energy production using a neural network and Supporting Vector Machines (SVM). The article proposes the selection of a training set and the possibility of combining models in a complementary hybrid model.

articleTitle: Integration of Application Employed for Balance Difference Analysis with Network Asset Management and Measurement Data Management Systems in a Large Distribution Company
abstract: An application SORB is based on the statistical method of calculation of electric energy losses in distribution networks. The application Bi-sun has got new possibilities and functionalities last time which enable it's cooperation with the network assets managing system and central measurements database.

articleTitle: Automatic fault location at lines with trilateral feed
abstract: Algorithms for automatic detection of the location of short circuits on overhead lines with a different number of power sources are proposed. The algorithms use the full values and the symmetrical components of the mode parameters from all sides of the line. If necessary, the replacement circuit of the line to the scheme of two-sided power is performed by equivalenting the parameters. The calculation in accordance with the method based on the use of the parameters of the direct sequence equivalent circuit and the constituent parameters of the direct sequence mode does not depend on the type of short circuit (SC). In the method based on the principle of remote relay protection, calculations are performed depending on the type of short circuit. For the technical implementation of automatic fault location, Regina recorders are used, which are installed at the hub substations. Synchronization of measurement parameters of the mode is performed by the GPS signal. The necessary information about the mode parameters from different sides of the line is transmitted to the server, which calculates the distance to the point of damage. Analysis of the accuracy of determining the location of damage is made on the basis of information about the real damage to the air lines. The assessment of the influence of the main factors on the accuracy of determining the location of damage.

articleTitle: Analysis of Load Profiles for Forming Energy Clusters Purpose
abstract: The variety of loads and sources of electricity in terms of power variation are fundamental importance for determining the possibility of balancing electricity (long-term) as well as balancing power (short-term) in the planned area of the energy cluster's operation. One of the steps for creating an energy cluster should be the analysis of electricity consumption profiles. Due to the increasing number of meters with remote reading (Automatic Meter Reading or Advanced Metering Infrastructure) installed at the LV consumers (IV and V connection group), which also enable acquisition and archiving of energy consumption data over long periods of time, it is possible to rely on actual measurement data for creating real load profiles. Due to the current poor access to the actual measurement data for the purpose of creating balances, for this group of consumers, the standard electricity consumption profiles of various types of loads are used. The standard electricity consumption profiles creating and publishing is required from the Distribution system operator. The paper presents the analysis of real profiles of various types of low voltage consumers (belonging to the fourth and fifth connection group) compared to standard profiles. The results of analyzes can be useful in creating energy clusters to provide balancing electricity in their operation area.

articleTitle: Managing the operation of a prosumer installation by using an energy storage system
abstract: The article concerns the analysis of the work of low-voltage prosumer installation consisting of receivers and sources of electricity. The tested system imitates the electrical installation of a hypothetical customer, working with a variable load and variable energy production. The main technical problems related to the operation of such an installation are presented. The use of an electric energy storage system in the installation, whose purpose is to manage the active power of a prosumer installation, has been considered. The basic criterion of the system operation is the reduction of costs incurred by the owner. The efficiency of the energy storage system was tested by means of a simulation model developed in the PSCAD/EMTDC program. Sample results of the simulation are presented.

articleTitle: Improving Adequacy of Simulation Transitional Processes in Electric Systems by More Comprehensive Consideration Phenomena in Circuit-Breakers
abstract: Computer simulation is the main tool for studying transitional processes in electric power systems including switching transitions of high-voltage system's equipment such as transformers and autotransformers, power capacitor banks, power transmission lines etc. In this regard ensuring adequacy of the models and methods used becomes very important. In general the satisfactory adequacy of computer simulation can be reached by two principal ways. One of them is comprehensive consideration of all the physical phenomena might have notable influence on the process under consideration. For the problem under study these are chopping of switched-off current and arcs' repeated re-strikes and re-ignitions in circuit-breakers, arc resistance etc. Another one is providing stability of transitional functions of voltages and currents due to use appropriate ode solvers and algorithms and also simulation parameters ensuring convergence of solutions. The paper presents results of investigation influence of arc resistance and inertia of current chopping process (slope of chop current) on functions of transitional voltages at switching-off unloaded transformer and unloaded power transmission line by SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> and vacuum circuit-breakers. The research curried-out allowed us to estimate influence of arc resistance and inertia of the current chopping process on transitional voltages. There was done quantitative estimation of transitional voltages deviations conditioned by ignoring of the phenomena of arc and the gradual decline of the chop current in the circuit-breaker.

articleTitle: Automated PMU accuracy analysis based on TTCN-3 system architecture
abstract: The reliable, safe and continues delivery of energy to consumers is the main success indicator of power grid. New challenges for system appear such as integration of more Renewable Energy Sources (RES), deregulation of the electricity market, new network users and active participation of energy consumers. Power grids need, therefore, a proper system protection and control as well as measurements for monitoring ability. The devices, which can offer synchronized, precise measurements to enhance the system observability are Phasor Measurement Units (PMUs). For the practical application of these modern devices in the power grids, they have to be tested in accordance with applicable standards. In this paper, the automated testing procedure of PMU accuracy verification in accordance to IEEE standard has been proposed. The test bench scheme and developed testing system architecture are based on TTCN-3. The results of the two devices tests are given.

articleTitle: Development of intellectual information-measuring system for Azerbaijan power system regime reliability control
abstract: One of the most important tasks of ensuring regime reliability of the Azerbaijan PS in the conditions of development and its parallel work in the structure of a large Association is the improvement of the existing information-measuring system of CAA (Counter Accident Automation) and CAC (Counter Accident Control) on the basis of the WAMS system and its integration with the SCADA/EMS system.

articleTitle: Using historical utility outage data to compute overall transmission grid resilience
abstract: Given increasing risk from climate-induced natural hazards, there is growing interest in the development of methods that can quantitatively measure resilience in power systems. This work quantifies resilience in electric power transmission networks in a new and comprehensive way that can represent the multiple processes of resilience. A novel aspect of this approach is the use of empirical data to develop the probability distributions that drive the computational model. This paper demonstrates the approach by measuring the impact of one potential improvement to a power system. Specifically, we measure the impact of additional distributed generation (DG) on power system resilience, and find that DG can substantially increase resilience.

articleTitle: Vehicle to Grid as an Important Element of the Energy Community
abstract: 1. The article presents the role that V2G technology could play in the energy community. Its potential for the energy community needs will be estimated on the basis of analytical and experimental analysis (case study results). Barriers limiting the possibility of widespread use of such solutions will also be indicated.

articleTitle: Assessment of General Feasibility for Robust Islanding
abstract: Intentional islanding is a concept where power system is divided, in case of a significant disturbance, into smaller segments in order to prevent a complete black-out. In this paper the results of three different approaches to assess the feasibility of intentional islanding is presented using generic power system model. The study targets to identify on high level the criteria for successful islanding based on the system's main characteristics with a wide variety of operating conditions. The operating conditions were executed by varying size of the studied system, imbalance level at the time of islanding and the response speed of the turbine governor. The conditions were derived so that they can be considered to represent on a general level, the possible regional islands and their generation portfolio in Finland. Size of the possible regional islands was represented by varying the kinetic energy of the rotating masses. The results showed that the frequency response stayed within tolerable limits when the total imbalance was maximum of 1.25 % of the total kinetic energy of the rotating masses, i.e. very a narrow range of the studied combinations. Based on the results, it can also be concluded that turbine speed control parameters, tuned for certain size of system, do not likely perform in an adequate manner when the rotational kinetic energy of the systems varies. Considering the results of the study, it seems that the required combinations for robust island may be very rarely available because of the present market-based electricity generation allocation and configuration. However, separate system specific studies to address the possibility of intentional islanding should be performed considering the actual availability and variations of generation and the actual power system configurations.

articleTitle: Reliability Models of Generating Units Utilizing Renewable Energy Sources
abstract: The article presents the ways of modelling unstable (variable) renewable energy sources in calculations of reliability of power systems. Basic reliability models of generating units have been described. Two reliability categories, which are related to variable renewable energy sources, were distinguished: structural reliability and production reliability. Algorithms of the proceedings in creating a multi-state reliability model of wind power plants, solar power plants and small hydroelectric power plants are presented.

articleTitle: Enhanced generation, energy storage and transmission expansion planning for renewables with operational flexibility through unit commitment
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the impact of operational flexibility in planning context considering four operational models; Economic Dispatch (ED), ED with ramping, Unit Commitment (UC) and UC with convex relaxation (UC-C). Using these operational models and three test cases; 6, 14, 24 bus systems, we quantity the error that occur due to exclusion or approximation of flexibility c onstraints. Numerical analysis reveals that this error in total cost can be as high as 8% and that approximated operational models such as ED, ED+R or UC-C could provide sub-optimal solutions with inefficient capacity mix. Even though the impact of sub-optimal solutions is minor in the observed set of experiments, this could be problem specific. As these solutions are driven by multiple factors such as network topology, candidate availability and other input parameters, a constrained system with limited options is more likely to be affected by approximated operational flexibility.

articleTitle: Selected aspects of energy efficiency – the case study Poland
abstract: This paper shows issue of energy efficiency on example of Poland. Analysis and assessment of selected aspects of energy efficiency in Poland is shown. National and the European Union legal regulations which describe energy efficiency, are discussed. Support programmes and measures aimed at improving energy efficiency at the national, regional and local levels are shown. Problem of energy efficiency of national economy are shown. Conclusions contain analysis of perspectives of development of energy efficiency increase in Poland in the future.

articleTitle: Technological Conditions for VSC and LCC HVDC Systems in Reference to Network Code Requirements
abstract: High voltage HVDC systems are widely used in power system. This also applies to the National Power System in which in the near future construction of another HVDC system between Lithuania and Poland, and in the long term a DC connection with Denmark are planned. HVDC systems are complex electrical power objects with specific properties. They may have different properties and different functionalities depending on the technology used. This paper provides a synthetic overview of HVDC systems in relation to two key technologies of their implementation, VSC and LCC. This review was made from the point of view of meeting the requirements of the HVDC network code.

Author Keywords: High Voltage Direct Current Transmission Systems
